question.text: Following the November 18, 2024 amendments to the AIF Regulations on pro-rata and pari-passu rights, which of the following CLASS of entities may subscribe to a junior/subordinate class of units accepting lesser returns or higher losses in Category II AIFs?

answer.text: Any high-net-worth individual with AI status
Any mutual fund investing above INR 100 crore
Only the fund's employees and directors

The Manager/Sponsor of the AIF; Multilateral/Bilateral DFIs; State Industrial Development Corporations; entities owned or controlled by Central/State Government or foreign Governments (including central banks and SWFs)

explanation.text: The Logic: The following entities may subscribe to a junior/subordinate class of units in Cat I/II AIFs and accept lesser returns or excess losses: (i) Manager or Sponsor of the AIF; (ii) Multilateral or Bilateral Development Financial Institutions; (iii) State Industrial Development Corporations; (iv) entities established, owned or controlled by Central/State Government or foreign Governments, including Central Banks and Sovereign Wealth Funds. If the Manager/Sponsor subscribes to the junior class, no evergreening of their loans via investee companies is permitted. The Trap: Options A/B/C propose classes that cannot subscribe to subordinated units. HNIs and MFs, regardless of size, are not in this list. The anti-evergreening rule specifically restricts Manager/Sponsor self-dealing. Note: Workbook pages 362-363 contain the junior/subordinate class list and the differential-rights principles.
